hidden-phase.alt: Two panels compare return-time sensitivity when zero, one, two, four or all future turns are preserved at each cell.
hidden-phase.caption: Hidden-phase pilot: mean absolute log-two time changes with four-start standard deviations. The support gate failed in most start/area groups; these selected long excursions do not establish a transport mechanism.

mechanics.alt: Successive grid diagrams showing an ant turning, changing the cell colour and stepping forward.
mechanics.caption: Read the rule one colour at a time: turn left or right, advance the cell’s colour, then move. These small deterministic examples explain the instructions behind every experiment.

gallery.alt: A gallery comparing the colour patterns and territory shapes produced by different ant rules.
gallery.caption: A few instructions can produce very different worlds. This is a selected gallery, not a measure of how often each kind of behaviour occurs; rule labels identify the examples.

exponents.alt: Distributions of fitted width and gyration-radius exponents for compact ant rules and rotor controls, with a one-third reference line.
exponents.caption: The crowded peak near one third is the puzzle. Each histogram summarizes finite-window fits; the rotor control shows why a fitted peak is evidence to investigate, rather than a proof of an exact exponent. Census ants are single runs per rule, while rotor samples vary the initial arrows.

edge.alt: An ant territory and an enlarged patch with visited boundary cells outlined in black.
edge.caption: The boundary is the set of visited cells next to unvisited ground, including hole rims. The zoom makes the measurement concrete: time spent on those cells and the chance of discovering a neighbour are different parts of growth.

rotor.alt: Visit-density maps for a rotor and ant RLL, followed by their radial profiles scaled by territory radius and visits per cell.
rotor.caption: Both walkers revisit the older centre more heavily. The scaled radial profiles compare accumulated visits, not instantaneous occupation. A cone can follow from occupation and growth assumptions without explaining why that growth law holds.

boundary-factors.alt: Fresh-ground entry probability c and normalized boundary occupation kappa against log2 time for six long ant trajectories.
boundary-factors.caption: Two ways to grow slowly: rarely reach the edge, or rarely discover fresh ground when there. The lines track those factors in six long trajectories. Their decomposition is a diagnostic; reconstructing the same run’s growth does not establish a mechanism.

late-switch.alt: RLRLLL switches from expensive blob growth to column sweeping; the lower panels show a period-three wake, back-and-forth motion and two sweep predictions.
late-switch.caption: Read the upper panel as the cost of a new cell: after the late switch it drops sharply. Below, the colour wake and sawtooth motion reveal the column sweep. The two prediction checks describe this phase of one deterministic trajectory; they do not identify what triggers it.

memory-paths.alt: Selected paths of walkers with different local memory rules.
memory-paths.caption: Memory is not one mechanism. These selected trajectories show how changing the way a walker remembers visited ground changes its exploration. The accompanying growth measurements, rather than appearance alone, determine the comparison.

memory-growth.alt: Growth comparisons among ants and several simpler walkers with local memory.
memory-growth.caption: The toy walkers test whether a simpler form of local memory reproduces the observed growth. These finite runs compare particular implementations, not every possible self-interacting walk.

fixed-area.alt: Independent-seed excursion-tail cutoff versus boundary occupation at visited areas 32768 and 131072; the negative association is stronger at the larger area.
fixed-area.caption: Each panel compares rules at a fixed visited area, with separate seeds for the long-excursion statistic and boundary occupation. Longer extreme excursions accompany lower boundary occupation more clearly in the larger territory. The primary small-area criterion fails; the selected 44-rule cohort does not establish causality. Seeds, bands and uncertainty are recorded in the experiment record.

alpha-gap.alt: The distribution of fitted growth exponents and checks of the cut between slow and compact growers.
alpha-gap.caption: The cut separates a slow-growth population from the compact-growth peak. Moving it changes the central estimate little, but not little enough to pass the strict registered tolerance. A statistical trough is not proof of a phase boundary.

occupancy-home.alt: Saved multi-panel colour and occupancy analysis of tethered rule RRRRRLLLLLL.
occupancy-home.caption: The territory is larger than the neighbourhood where this ant spends most of its time. Compare the colour field with occupancy and the page’s motion diagnostics. This is a selected saved example; the individual panel labels give its measurement context.

occupancy-blob.alt: Saved multi-panel colour and occupancy analysis of compact-growing rule RLR.
occupancy-blob.caption: A compact grower provides a comparison with the tethered example. The visit-density and motion panels ask how the walker uses its territory, which a colour snapshot alone cannot reveal. This is descriptive context, not an independent test of every linked experiment.

crystal.alt: Visit-count image of rule RLLLLRRL showing long diagonal structures.
crystal.caption: The long diagonal rays make the crystal question visible. This is the saved visit image of the deterministic blank-board rule RLLLLRRL; the ray tests in the record distinguish the visible structure from claims about how it sustains itself.

snapshot.alt: Saved colour-field snapshot of the symmetric builder LLRR.
snapshot.caption: LLRR is a reminder that an ant need not build an irregular blob. This selected saved snapshot is visual context; use the generating record for its run parameters rather than inferring a growth exponent from the shape.

excursion-cup-010.alt: CCDF of cup-walker excursion durations coloured by window-end L, shown under tau/L and tau/L-squared scalings.
excursion-cup-010.caption: Revision-1 primary reflecting cup (stay-on-reject, p frozen before Scores). Collapse Score preferred the sweep scaling; confirmation was not run.

excursion-cup-compactness.alt: Two panels: isoperimetric proxy A over P squared and linear size L versus window index for three frozen cup probabilities.
excursion-cup-compactness.caption: Cup compactness diagnostics: L grows, but the frozen filled-blob cut on A/P squared fails for every reported p.

excursion-mf-rev1.alt: CCDF of mean-field excursion durations under tau/L and tau/L-squared with fresh Revision-1 seeds.
excursion-mf-rev1.caption: Revision-1 mean-field L-control: Score still prefers the sweep scaling under the frozen margin.
